editorial:
Imagine a world where money and power can buy anything, and everyone is just trying to get a piece of the pie. You are dropped into a wild, flashy version of Italy between 2006 and 2010, centering on a man who behaves like a walking paradise. He is based on Silvio Berlusconi, and the movie shows the strange crowd of people who orbit around him. You will meet ambitious assistants and hopeful young women who all want to be close to his wealth. The vibe is totally over-the-top and feels like a colorful dream where the rules of right and wrong just do not exist. It is a look at a time that was decadent and kind of messy, but also full of energy.

What really pops is the acting and the beautiful shots of luxury homes and fancy parties. The pacing is a bit slow because it feels more like a collection of portraits than a straight story, but that is part of the charm. If you like movies that feel like a fancy art gallery, you will love this. It is a bit weird, but it keeps you curious.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing the cycle of power and how it never truly stops. You see the man continue to surround himself with new, younger faces as he tries to stay relevant and powerful. It wraps up by showing that while the people around him change, his hunger for attention stays the same. There is no big shock twist, but rather a sad realization that this lifestyle of greed and fake beauty just keeps repeating itself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about power, wealth, and strange personalities.
